chapter: Rising in Manhattan: clubs, Hilda and the Latin scene
title: Writing "Paella"
summary: Insulted when promoter Federico Pagani asked if he had tried paella, he wrote the tune on the subway.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I see. What about Paella now? Ahh, Paella happens to be a seafood with Spanish rice.
Did you like seafood at the time?
I love it, I love it .....
.....but this is funny thing about it too. I, you know Federico Pagani?
A promoter, he is one is responsible all this things that are happened now, ahn we used to work together. We used to promote together because he was the original director of the ......

.......Montecino Happy Boys, but they had a misunderstanding, so he was out, so we got together. We - Federico, we used to organize dances all over the place, so one day he was coming out of a restaurant and we were talking and I say: "Federico, hello, how are you?" He said: "Bueno, I just had a paella. Did you ever try a paella before"? You know, I got insulted, I said, huh this guy, "I know how to make paella. How you going to ask me if I ever taste it, a paella?" So I went in the subway that particular day, that it was a matinee at La Conga, and I wrote "Paella" in the train.
